# orionbelt Provider

Manage an Orion Belt access gateway.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    orionbelt = {
      source = "orion-belt-dev/orionbelt"
    }
  }
}

# The API key is read from ORIONBELT_API_KEY when api_key is not set.
provider "orionbelt" {
  url = "https://orion.example.com"

  compliance {
    frameworks         = ["soc2", "pci-dss-4"]
    max_grant_duration = "720h"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) Admin or operator API key. Defaults to ORIONBELT_API_KEY.
- `ca_cert_pem` (String) PEM CA bundle that signs the gateway's TLS certificate. Replaces the system roots.
- `compliance` (Block, Optional) Compliance frameworks every resource must satisfy. Plans and applies fail on any violation. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--compliance))
- `insecure_http` (Boolean) Allow a plain http:// URL. Only for local labs: the API key is sent in clear text.
- `timeout` (String) Per-request timeout as a Go duration. Default 30s.
- `url` (String) Gateway base URL, e.g. https://orion.example.com. Defaults to ORIONBELT_URL.

<a id="nestedblock--compliance"></a>
### Nested Schema for `compliance`

Optional:

- `denied_remote_users` (List of String) Remote accounts no grant may name, in addition to the frameworks' list.
- `frameworks` (List of String) Frameworks to enforce: soc2, iso27001, pci-dss-4.
- `max_grant_duration` (String) Tighter limit on how far in the future a grant may expire, e.g. 8h or 720h.
